notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 6 simply supported 20-ft bays, W27X146 girders, one 25-ton cab crane, on column caps over new W14X145 crane columns beside the existing W14X159 building columns (pinned bases, anchor rods and spread footings, crane-level rod X-bracing between the crane columns), with the rail, the top-flange ties and the column ties to the building columns, bearings and end stops; the building columns are checked for the tie forces with their existing load effects and carry no runway vertical load. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 9.53, flange-tie-saddle-fatigue 2.84 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class A); on a crane column the top flange is tied to the building column, a flexible restraint: the girder twists more at the supports, and a welded saddle on the tied flange is a Category D/E attachment in that flange lateral bending): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 9.53, flange-tie-saddle-fatigue 2.84 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class A); on a crane column the top flange is tied to the building column, a flexible restraint: the girder twists more at the supports, and a welded saddle on the tied flange is a Category D/E attachment in that flange lateral bending): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, H1 top-flange interaction with the load-height LTB strength ratio 0.76, vertical deflection 0.29, lateral 0.36 and rail-head movement with twist 0.71 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 23 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W18X143: tips ratio 1.08 > 0.85; rail-head movement with twist 1.12 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New crane column for a 25-ton crane (W12X65 to 7.5 t, W14X90 to 15 t, W14X109 to 30 t, else W14X132), pinned base, braced at the cap across the runway by the column tie and along it by the crane-level bracing. The W14X109 crane column gives member (H1) ratio 0.39, bracing connection (column web at the gussets and strut tabs, stiffened) ratio 0.92, column cap ratio 1.29: the column cap exceeds 1.00 and no local fix brings it there; the lightest heavier W14 that passes.

Fictitious example existing building column for a 25-ton crane (W14X90 to 7.5 t, W14X120 to 15 t, W14X159 to 30 t, else W14X211), checked for the tie forces with its existing load effects; replace with the surveyed shape.

selections.designed: combined with the building column, 102 in square; 150 in at the braced columns
selections.reason: Isolated 13 ft square crane-column footings 29.5 in from the building column would be 78.5 in into its 5 ft footing (6 in clear required): each crane column and its building column stand on one combined footing replacing the existing one, 8.5 ft square (12.5 ft at the braced columns), the building column shored and re-set on new anchor rods; sized for the base reactions; the braced columns' footing apart from the others' (the rods' uplift and shear along the runway), sliding resisted by the base friction and the soil's lateral bearing on the footing and its shear key (IBC §1806.3.1).

Column tie 0.5 in × 8 in with 2 0.75 in A325 bolts on sleeves in 1.375 in × 1.875 in vertical slots: the lightest within the 0.9 sizing target for the estimated column-tie force 25.032 kip (the girder bottom-flange force through the cap, bounded by the girder tie force estimate 23.532 kip; the crane column's eccentric top reaction 0.101 kip; the brace force 0.01P_r 1.399 kip; the calculation takes the bottom-flange force from the girder model) and its fatigue range 12.5 kip at all cycles; slot travel 0.272 in each way (the larger column shortening plus the erection tolerance).

The building column face from the girder web (the crane-column centerline): at least the crane column's half depth plus the column tie's clear gap, moved out by the tie sizing (to at most 30 in) where the tie needs the flexible length; the crane column stands 14.6 in clear of the building column.

Weld-on clip bases on the top flange are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 13.27 ksi (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 2,000,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 10.32 ksi (ratio 1.29, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
